title: Assessing Myogenic Tone and Perfusion Pressure in Isolated Mouse Kidneys
author: Chu, Kassmann, et al.

steps.title: Prepare glass cannula
steps.instruction: Fabricate a glass cannula with an inner tip diameter of 0.3–0.4 mm using a micropipette puller.

substeps.instruction: Install the glass tube into the puller head and adjust positioning.
Set both puller scales to 0.
Turn on the heater; let the lower scale descend to 4 mm, fix the lower holder, then turn the heater off.
Adjust the upper scale to 3.5 mm, turn the heater on again and pull until the tube separates into two parts.
Remove the longer cannula, trim excess glass, and polish the surface with a smooth metal tool (e.g., forceps).
Verify that the inner diameter is between 0.3 mm and 0.4 mm.

steps.title: Oxygenate solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare and oxygenate all perfusion solutions for at least 15 minutes before kidney isolation.

substeps.instruction: Set a water bath to 37 °C.
Place physiological salt solution (PSS) and 60 mM KCl solution in the bath.
Insert carbogen gas tubes (95 % O₂, 5 % CO₂) into each solution bottle.
Place a small bottle of PSS on ice and connect it to carbogen.

steps.title: Set up perfusion equipment
steps.instruction: Configure the temperature controller, pressure monitor, peristaltic pump, and data‑acquisition software.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the chamber temperature controller and set it to 37 °C (module 8).
Switch on the pressure monitor (module 2) and the peristaltic pump (module 4).
Fill the entire tubing system with the oxygenated solution, pause the pump, and set the pressure monitor to 0 mm Hg.
Open LabChart, set the pressure measurement range, and define the number of chambers (4).

steps.title: Isolate mouse kidneys
steps.instruction: Excise both kidneys from a sacrificed mouse and keep them in cold oxygenated PSS.

substeps.instruction: Open the abdominal cavity, displace intestine and liver leftward to expose the kidneys.
Transect connective tissue, the abdominal aorta, and the inferior vena cava above the kidneys.
Using forceps, lift the lower pole of the right kidney and dissect dorsal connective tissue from bottom to top with scissors.
Repeat the dissection on the left kidney and move the left kidney to the right side.
Grab the abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava at the level of the lower kidney and cut them.
Delicately separate aorta and vena cava from underlying muscle/connective tissue.
Transfer the excised kidneys into a plate containing cold, oxygenated PSS solution.

steps.title: Isolate renal arteries
steps.instruction: Expose and free the renal arteries from surrounding tissue while preserving the aortic segment.

substeps.instruction: Fix adipose tissue at the upper and lower margins of each kidney with needles to maintain slight tension on the renal artery.
Trim excess abdominal aorta distal to the renal arteries.
Make an upward incision along the inferior vena cava toward the 11 o’clock position.
Extend the incision to the right renal vein to visualize the right renal artery; repeat for the left side.
Using scissors, remove connective and perivascular adipose tissue surrounding the renal arteries and aorta.
Separate the two renal arteries from the aorta.
